title: A World Built. A Failure Kept.

recording.edit: Scene-only crop; historical stat board removed. Spatial downscale and H264 re-encode; source cadence retained.

arms.label: Qwen 27B MLX 8-bit · Mac
repairs: renamed duplicate top-level identifier `_s` (scratch Vector3) to `_sv` (2 lines); original preserved as mac-8bit-original.html

arms.label: aeon-nvfp4-attempt2-clienttimeout-dnf
arms.detail: non-streaming urllib client hit timeout=3600s while server was still generating; vLLM aborted request on disconnect; no tokens recovered. Fix: switched run_arm.py to SSE streaming (continuous bytes -> no idle-socket timeout) with partial-progress file.

arms.label: aeon-nvfp4-attempt3-degeneration-dnf
arms.detail: reasoning completed cleanly (58,688 chars) but content degenerated at ~15K chars into a repetition loop: 'const vTop/vMain/vWall/vPond = new (Group);' cycle x1098 with progressive token decay (THREE.Group -> TH.Group -> Group); 117K of 132K content chars are loop output; no </body>/</html>; finish_reason=stop after 67,714 tokens. First genuine MODEL failure (attempts 1-2 were harness: 32K cap, client timeout). Settings identical to other arms.

arms.label: aeon-nvfp4-attempt4-nocontent-dnf
arms.detail: second genuine model failure, distinct mode: thinking completed (55,334 chars, ~19.8K tokens) then model emitted EOS with ZERO content — never began the artifact. finish=stop at 19,815 tokens, 115K of budget unused. Combined with attempt 3 (degeneration loop), AEON NVFP4 is 0/2 on this task under the matched contract (xhigh, temp 0.7, thinking ON). Attempts 1-2 were harness faults, not counted.

notes: Successful displayed runs requested thinking ON, xhigh, temperature 0.7 and a 120,000-token output budget. Different model variants and engines mean this is not a controlled quantization-only experiment.

AEON attempts 1–2 failed because of harness limits (an output cap and a client timeout). Attempts 3–4 are distinct model failures: repetitive degeneration, then a natural stop with no final content. These must not be counted as four model failures.
The Mac scene includes a two-line duplicate-identifier repair. Flash-Next has no recorded repair. This excerpt preserves the original recordings’ motion; it is not a rendering-FPS benchmark.
